description:
We’re UGrowth, a team building tools that help city farmers grow more food with less water, healthier soil and less guesswork. Our project uses NASA Earth observation data to suggest crop rotations that cope with a changing climate.

We’re interested in agriculture, climate, data and building practical things people actually use. Between us we cover software development, data analysis and business planning, and we care about turning space data into real impact on the ground.
summary: UGrowth Planner is a web app that helps city and peri-urban farmers in Indonesia. The farmer enters a location, planting month, soil (pH, texture, organic matter), water source, current crop and priorities: profit, water, soil health and climate risk. The app pulls temperature, rainfall, sunlight and soil wetness from NASA POWER (MERRA-2 and CERES), estimates crop water needs with FAO-56 coefficients, and checks 56 local crops month by month for heat, elevation, soil and rain risk. It then compares thousands of rotations and recommends plans scored on income, irrigation, soil health and resilience, with a bad-year test for El Niño, La Niña and a hotter 2040s. In our Jakarta example, the recommended plan kept income level with chili all year, raised soil health from 8 to 79 and cut watering by about 40%. The goal is to make Jakarta and other cities less dependent on food from outside, cut water use and protect soil. We built it as an offline-capable, mobile-friendly HTML, CSS and JavaScript app with Python data scripts, NASA POWER, FAO EcoCrop and Kementan data, and Claude assisted with coding and research. What makes it different is that it puts income next to soil and water results in plain language. Throughout, we considered small urban plots, El Niño, limited water, market gluts and being honest about estimated data.
